description: Manhattan Associates, Inc. develops, sells, deploys, services, and maintains software solutions to manage supply chains, inventory, and omni-channel operations. It offers warehouse management solution
description_full: Manhattan Associates, Inc. develops, sells, deploys, services, and maintains software solutions to manage supply chains, inventory, and omni-channel operations. It offers warehouse management solution for managing goods and information across the distribution centers; Manhattan Active Warehouse Management, a cloud native and version less application for the associate; and transportation management solution for helping shippers navigate their way through the demands and meet customer service expectations at the lowest possible freight costs; Manhattan SCALE, a portfolio of logistics execution solution; and Manhattan Active Omni, which offers order management, store inventory and fulfillment, call center, POS, and customer engagement tools for enterprises and stores. The company also provides demand forecasting and replenishment, allocation, and unified business planning; technology platform including Manhattan Active Platform solutions, a cloud-native product designed to provide version-less product access; maintenance services, which offers on-premises software licensees with software upgrades for additional or improved functionality and technological advances; and professional services, such as solutions planning and implementation, and related consulting services. In addition, it provides training and change management services; and resells computer hardware, radio frequency terminal networks, radio frequency identification chip readers, bar code printers and scanners, and other peripherals. The company offers products through direct sales personnel and partnership agreements with various organizations. It serves retail, consumer goods, food and grocery, logistics service providers, industrial and wholesale, high technology and electronics, life sciences, and government industries. The company operates in the Americas, Europe, the Middle East, Africa, and the Asia Pacific. Manhattan Associates, Inc. was founded in 1990 and is headquartered in Atlanta, Georgia.

financial_summary: Manhattan Associates, Inc. is a large-cap technology business with a $14.9B market cap on $1.1B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +12% over the past three years and +23% annually across the full decade, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder.
Returns on capital run at 1059% against a 10% cost of capital — a 1049-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat.

The business throws off $374M in free cash flow — roughly 35 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.77× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and interest coverage of 40× is fortress-like.

Shareholder yield of 2.1% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and stock-based comp at 10% of revenue is silent dilution an owner has to account for, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome.

sect: Its 26% operating margin runs 19pp above the Technology median (7%), a real cost or pricing edge over peers.
Its share of sector profits slightly exceeds its share of revenue (1.11x).
Over five years it has been gaining share of the sector profit pool (+2.5% a year).
The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.03 across 533 companies in the universe; the top four hold 29% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
mkt: The shares are in a strong uptrend, up 26% over the past year excluding the latest month.
The price sits near the top of its 52-week range, 2% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 47% and a beta of 1.15, it moves roughly with the market, though its beta has shifted (1y 0.63 vs 5y 1.21), so read it loosely.
Liquidity is deep, with about $133.5M traded a day.
In past sell-offs it fell 58% in the 2020 crash, 30% in the 2022 bear market and 48% in 2008.
val: The price sits above its DCF fair value of $123 (margin of safety -109%), so there is no valuation cushion.
The fair-value models disagree (dispersion 49%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $88.22 to $176 (P10-P90), so treat the estimate as noisy.
On multiples it looks expensive against Technology peers: P/E 72.0 vs 27.4, EV/EBITDA 50.1 vs 17.1 and P/FCF 39.9 vs 26.1 (sector median).
Against its own history it is dear: the EBIT multiple sits 24% above its 10-year median.
Earnings yields are thin: an FCF yield of 2.5% (below the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 1.9% (vs the 8% bar).
The 10 covering analysts target $276 on average, 7% above the price, well away from the model's fair value.
prof: ROIC of 1059% clears the cost of capital of 10.3% by 1049pp, the mark of a value creator; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 2.14).
It converts 35% of revenue into free cash flow, or 24% after stock compensation.
Earnings quality looks solid: cash conversion of 1.77x.
ROE of 70% comes mostly from margins and asset turnover rather than leverage (2.7x equity multiplier).
It spends 13.4% of revenue on R&D and 10.3% on stock compensation (above the 2% gate).
hlth: The balance sheet carries net cash of $328.7M (2% of market cap).
growth: Revenue has compounded at 12.1% over 3 years, 13.0% over 5 years and 23.5% over 10 years, and it has been lumpy (year-to-year swings of 95%).
At current returns, reinvesting 16% of profits supports about 30.0% a year of fundamental growth, enough to sustain growth.
Free cash flow has compounded 22.0% a year over five years.
Forward indicators: a book-to-bill of 1.37 (orders outpacing sales), a backlog worth 2.0x annual revenue and deferred revenue up 21%.
Capex runs 2.4x depreciation (1.4% of sales), so it is building capacity for future growth.
Its Rule of 40 score is 37, below the 40 that marks a healthy growth business.
own: Insiders own a modest 1.4%, and reported institutional holdings exceed 100% of shares (a sign of heavy share lending).
Insiders have only sold over the past year (6 sales, net $3.4M sold).
It returns 2.1% a year to shareholders (2.1% in buybacks).
The share count has shrunk 1.7% a year over five years, steadily raising each holder's stake.
people: With about 3,980 employees, each generates about $272K of revenue, 0.7x the Technology median, and revenue has grown 8.9% a year across its filed history.
That works out to $94K of free cash flow per employee.
CEO pay is $3.7M (14x revenue per employee).
